model: Titan 3-DOF reference-column entry; not an official Dragonfly EDL prediction

initial_location.frame: IAU_TITAN text-PCK; planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude
initial_location.note: Body-fixed state subpoint, not a landing prediction. Rotating-frame speed omits winds.

final_location.frame: IAU_TITAN text-PCK; planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude
final_location.note: Body-fixed state subpoint, not a landing prediction. Rotating-frame speed omits winds.

force_model: Spherical Titan gravity; aerodynamic force relative to rigidly rotating atmosphere plus specified winds; JPL-prescribed differential Saturn gravity.

metadata.model: Huygens HASI 2005 reference column; corrected archived ACC entry density and descent density
metadata.data_caveat: The entry profile TAB lacks density despite its label. Its 911 upper samples use the corrected HASI_L4_ACCE_DENSITY.TAB product at exactly matching altitudes; 1,816 lower samples retain the descent density product. No EOS-derived densities are needed in the bundled baseline.
metadata.interpolation: PCHIP of log density and log pressure; PCHIP temperature. The 146.797–157.3182 km gap is interpolated, not measured. Below the lowest 3 m, hold the lowest profile value to the surface.
limitations: A single 2005 reference column, not a forecast of Titan weather in 2034/2035.
No measured wind column is supplied here; baseline winds are zero relative to rigid corotation.
Archived entry densities are instrument-team retrievals from accelerometer deceleration; they inherit the original retrieval assumptions.
No uncertainty distribution is inferred from this single profile. Density scalings are sensitivity cases, not confidence intervals.
metadata.gram_upgrade: Titan-GRAM 2026 is available by request from https://software.nasa.gov/software/MFS-33888-1 ; CSV profiles can replace this reference column.

assumptions: Constant aeroshell ballistic coefficient; gamma=1.4 and constant 98% N2 / 2% CH4 gas constant for Mach estimates.
Zero lift by default. No six-DOF attitude, reefing, heating, ablation or terrain.
Drogue diameter 8.25 m and main diameter 16.7 m from NASA 2025; each CD=0.7 is an analyst assumption. Mass is held at the published CBE 2309 kg.

During drogue descent, assumed subsonic capsule CD=1.0 is retained. At 5 km main-chute drag replaces the combined model. No inflation, official drag database or mass-jettison model is included; release speed is computed, not fitted.
Stops at illustrative 800 m lander release; powered flight and touchdown are not propagated.
limitations: HASI is a single 2005 atmospheric column, not 2034/2035 weather.
No heat flux or thermal survivability prediction. Titan radiative heating cannot be replaced by an Earth heating formula.
No validated parachute/attitude/navigation database; full-descent mode is an illustrative scenario.
No powered flight, touchdown or landing ellipse prediction.

full_trajectory_join.coordinates: Heliocentric Ecliptic J2000; JD TDB, km, km/s

reference_load_check.note: Published Dragonfly study constraint compared with the simplified model; not a vehicle certification or survivability test.
